thread.title: Stock Market Rallies As Dow Jumps 330 Points, Techs Boost Nasdaq | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Stock Market Rallies As Dow Jumps 330 Points, Techs Boost Nasdaq | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks bounced back from a tough Thanksgiving week to boost the major indexes to big gains in the stock market today. The Nasdaq led amid a broad rally by beleaguered tech stocks.
X The Nasdaq soared 1.8%, the S&P 500 rallied 1.4% and the Dow Jones industrial average advanced 1.3%. Small caps also participated, with the Russell 2000 up nearly 1%.
Financial stocks led the Dow: American Express ( AXP ) rose 3%, while Visa ( V ), JPMorgan ( JPM ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) added more than 2% each. Big-cap techs including Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) also scored upside moves over 2%.
Apple ( AAPL ) reversed higher to a 0.5% gain. If it remains positive, that would halt a steep four-session slide. Shares remain 25% below their 52-week high and 11% below the 200-day moving average. Loop Capital Markets on Monday cut its price target on the iPhone maker to 225 from 259 but reiterated a buy rating. Apple has been under pressure since offering disappointing guidance Nov. 1.
Automakers, casino operators and internet retailers were among the top sector gainers in the stock market today. Tobacco, steel and food-related stocks underperformed.
Carmakers Cruise In Stock Market Today Tesla ( TSLA ) surged 5% as it shapes the right side of a base. It tried to break out Nov. 19, but reversed with the broader market to close below a 357.68 buy point. Since then, it's triggered the 7%-8% loss-cutting sell rule . But it also may be forming a new handle with a 366.85 entry.
Among other carmakers, Fiat Chrysler Automotive ( FCAU ) gapped up and rose 6% to retake its 50-day line. General Motors ( GM ) gained 5% to reclaim its 200-day average for the first time in five months. GM on Monday said it will double investments in electric and self-driving vehicles in the next two years. It also plans to halt production at several plants next year in order to focus on SUVs and trucks instead of sedans.

Please contact customer service CLOSE In the internet retail group, Amazon ( AMZN ) leapt 4%, boosted by Adobe Analytics data showing strong Black Friday online sales. China's JD.com ( JD ) popped 6%, while Etsy ( ETSY ) and Carvana ( CVNA ) rose nearly 5% apiece.
In the IBD 50, Trade Desk ( TTD ) outperformed with a 7% jump to retake its 50-day line for the first time since Oct. 9. Shares may be forming a base with potential buy point at 161.60.
Among other big gainers, Twitter ( TWTR ) rose 5%, while Atlassian ( TEAM ), HealthEquity ( HQY ) and CyberArk Software ( CYBR ) added more than 2% each.
The Innovator IBD 50 ETF ( FFTY ) climbed 1.4% as it tried for a third straight advance.
